chunks: If a debtor is in want, give him time until his circumstances improve; but if you forego (the debt) as charity, that will be to your good, if you really understand.

key_terms.ذُو عُسْرَةٍ: one who is in financial difficulty or poverty

ai.seo_question: What should a creditor do if a debtor is currently unable to pay their debt?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked with the subsequent verse (2:281) to highlight the divine accountability for debts, emphasizing that financial leniency is a spiritual investment. The term 'maysarah' (ease) is interpreted not merely as liquidity but as the debtor's capacity to repay without hardship, while 'sadaqah' implies a voluntary waiver of the principal as an act of piety. This instruction underscores the ethical obligation of creditors to prioritize mercy over strict legalism, a principle deeply valued in Islamic jurisprudence.
